voice: Rameses remains precise, reserved, and visibly flustered while Yvette uses polished, deliberate flirtation; standard spelling replaces phonetic accents without changing her leverage, his marriage, or the cult-room clue.

entries.text: ...Come a little closer, Monsieur Najeer. I want to show you something.
And what would that be, Miss Delacroix?
Look at the palm of my hand.
It is a lovely palm, certainly, but what am I supposed to see?
Do you see this line, Monsieur? It is my love line.
Good Lord, Miss Delacroix. It runs all the way up your arm and disappears beneath your sleeve.
Would you like to see where it ends, Rameses?
I... Well, that is... I am not quite sure how to answer.
Have you ever been to Paris, Rameses?
No. I cannot say that I have.
Then you have never seen the Eiffel Tower?
Then by all means, let me show you.
Miss Delacroix, please. I am a married man. Oh, dear.
Have you forgotten who let you into the museum, Rameses? Who showed you the secret room for your little ceremonies? You have not forgotten, have you?
Then you will let me give you the grand tour of the tower, yes?
We will have to go somewhere else. I do not feel safe here.
